caveats: Purposive bounded web-search sample; not random or nationally representative.

Four real scans are concentrated in two states and related filing families: two Vermont APA filings and two Tennessee GOC packets. They are distinct originals and distinct filings, but not four independent layout families.
Scans have embedded publisher OCR; this collection does not establish performance on image-only PDFs with no text layer.

Vermont cover forms are complete but larger rulemaking packages remain in original PDFs; runtime scope slice. Tennessee first-agency records retain complete supporting components and runtime scope unknown.
Louisiana, New Jersey and Oklahoma retain neighboring notices and runtime scope unknown; no target segmentation certification.
General-stratum quota was filled before later New Jersey and Delaware candidates; unused originals retained. No native-length exclusions or parser-success replacement occurred.

All48 planned searches were executed before queued-candidate downloads/inspection finished. This departs from a literal immediate-stop reading of the48-query ceiling; no unlisted queries or additional query rounds were used. Primary should review this collection-order deviation before freeze.

Search result order is recorded as returned; not every result was opened. First notice/form within each selected packet was used except the explicitly linked Idaho notice and the complete Arkansas notice within its supporting packet. Page selection is reviewer boundary work and is not a test of automatic register segmentation.
Native extraction, original PDF diagnostics and rendering ran locally; no OCR/parser-provider or model calls.
